review_comments: I notice MySQL [session_connect_attrs](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/performance-schema-session-connect-attrs-table.html) has definied PK. why we here do not need PK for the table?

It looks like none of the I_S and P_S tables have a primary key, so I followed that. Not sure if that's required or not. I also don't think having a PK makes a big difference here?

```
sql> select * from information_schema.KEY_COLUMN_USAGE WHERE CONSTRAINT_NAME='PRIMARY' AND table_schema='performance_schema';
Empty set (0.0048 sec)

sql> select * from information_schema.KEY_COLUMN_USAGE WHERE CONSTRAINT_NAME='PRIMARY' AND table_schema='information_schema';
Empty set (0.0042 sec)
```
if there is a little rows in this table, it is no big difference.
Why here set 10 Attributes? Can we use actual Attributes number column?

As `allAttrs` is a map of maps we would need to loop over all maps and get the sum of the lengths of all maps. Every map is one connection and often there are about 6 attributes per connection. So getting the exact map takes more CPU time while the less exact number might allocate more rows than needed, or would under allocate if there are many rows per connection.

```go
package main

import "testing"

func setup() map[uint64]map[string]string {
	m := make(map[uint64]map[string]string)
	for i := uint64(0); i < 100000; i++ {
		m[i] = map[string]string{
			"foo1": "bar",
			"foo2": "bar",
			"foo3": "bar",
			"foo4": "bar",
			"foo5": "bar",
			"foo6": "bar",
		}
	}
	return m
}

func BenchmarkSimple(b *testing.B) {
	m := setup()
	b.ResetTimer()
	println("Simple length of m: ", len(m)*10)
}

func BenchmarkExact(b *testing.B) {
	m := setup()
	b.ResetTimer()
	var t int
	for _, k := range m {
		t = t + len(k)
	}
	println("Exact length of m: ", t)
}
```
